html:
The movement, told in Greek tradition, of Dorian Greeks from the north into the Peloponnese around 1100 BCE, after the fall of the Mycenaean palaces. Myth called it the Return of the Heracleidae, the descendants of Heracles reclaiming their lands.

The Dorians spoke their own dialect and later held Sparta, Argos, Corinth, Crete and Rhodes. Classical Greeks used the story to explain why Dorians and Ionians lived where they did; the Ionian migration to Asia Minor was its mirror.

Modern scholars doubt there was one invasion. Archaeology shows no clear new culture arriving to wreck the palaces of Mycenaean Greece, which fell in the wider Late Bronze Age collapse. Dorian speakers may have drifted in slowly, or may have been there all along as a lower class. What is clear is that the Greek Dark Ages followed, with fewer people, no writing and simpler goods.
